runtimes: Kubernetes >=1.29 or OCI runtime with CAP_BPF+CAP_PERFMON

observation.coverage_basis: Configured kernel tracepoints observe selected exec/connect/openat activity inside the configured cgroup scope, including actions outside SDK instrumentation. Ring-buffer loss, sensor downtime, unsupported paths and scoping errors prevent an every-action guarantee. File access is off by default because openat volume is host-scale.

authentication.credential_handling: The emitter optionally reads a bearer-token file or a client certificate/key pair. TLS is the default; an explicit development-only insecure transport setting rejects bearer tokens and TLS files.

correlation_limitations: Kernel events carry pid/ppid/cgroup and timestamps — they are not span edges. Joining them to agent traces is inferred provenance, never causal.
Encrypted traffic yields metadata only: peer address, port, timing — never payload or trace headers.
Cgroup-to-workload attribution depends on the operator supplying the correct cgroup_path; mis-scoped filters observe the wrong boundary.

verification_evidence.claim: Covers minimized event translation, incomplete argv/path status, cgroup-scope validation, TLS configuration rejection, dedupe collapse, and rate limiting.
Linux Docker BPF capture test script; it must pass against the exact release image before live coverage is claimed and has not been qualified by local macOS tests.

known_blind_spots: Cannot identify prompts, completions, tool arguments, tool results, policy verdicts, or decision boundaries — kernel metadata only.
Requires CAP_BPF+CAP_PERFMON and kernel >=5.8 with BTF; the container runs read-only mounts and refuses to start on kernels that lack support.
Encrypted traffic prevents payload or trace-header inspection — peer/timing metadata only.
openat (file_access) is host-scale volume and off by default; enabling it without cgroup scoping can exceed emit budgets.
Attribution to a logical agent depends on correct cgroup_path; all_host=true is an explicit opt-in and widens collection to the whole node.
An adversarial workload with kernel-level access is outside this threat model — the emitter observes the host it runs on and cannot defend the kernel itself.
The emitter has a bounded fsynced source spool with at-least-once replay and stable record IDs, but neither source fsync nor OTLP acceptance proves durable destination storage.
Spool exhaustion causes a visible sensor stop; activity while the sensor is down or before a kernel loss count is durably queued cannot be reconstructed by this source.
Only configured tracepoints and cgroup scope are observed; kernel ring-buffer loss and partial argv/path capture require explicit incomplete status and independent reconciliation.
